subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks again for your time today, Alex — great conversation and appreciate the demo context. Per our call, below is a concise recap of the performance-related SLOs you mentioned, what we validated in the demo, and the recommended next steps (MAP) so we can move to a short pilot.

1) Customer SLOs (stated):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <= 300ms for single-turn text generation (critical paths).
- Streaming: first-byte streaming within 50ms of server response start for UI streaming UX.
- Throughput: target 500 requests/minute during peak, with sustained concurrency of ~50 concurrent sessions.
- Availability: 99.95% and regional failover for US production.

2) What we demoed today:
- Hosted API baseline: p95 token latency for a 256-token prompt at ~220ms in our NYC region (demo environment, cached prefixes).
- Streaming demo: token-by-token websocket stream with <60ms inter-token latency observed in the room (demo conditions).
- Autoscaling / Dedicated overview: showed Dedicated pool config for predictable concurrency and burst lanes.

3) Gaps / clarifications we need from FintechCo:
- Typical prompt size distribution (median and 95th token lengths).
- Expected request burst patterns (minute-by-minute at peak).
- Whether you require guaranteed p95 under cold cache vs warm cache.

4) Recommended technical next steps (MAP items):
- Action: FintechCo to send representative sample traffic (anonymized) + 1 hour peak trace. Owner: Alex. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Action: Redwood SE (Priyom) to run perf run against a Dedicated staging pool using your sample traffic; produce p50/p95/p99 and streaming first-byte times. Owner: Priyom. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Action: Align on decision criteria doc: what p95 number and streaming latency will be "sufficient" to proceed to pilot. Owner: Alex + Sean. Due: 2026-03-08.
- Action: Share SLO checklist + perf test harness. Owner: Marissa. Attached: slo_checklist.xlsx, perf-test-script.sh.

5) Quick notes on configuration suggestions (from demo):
- Use Dedicated with pre-warmed KV cache for high concurrency bursts; set autoscale headroom to 20% above expected peak.
- For streaming UX, prefer model variants with lower per-token compute (quantized profiles) and enable continuous batching tuned to your median prompt size.

If that all looks right, I'll kick off the SE perf run once we get the sample traffic. Please confirm the owner/duedates above or suggest edits.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: slo_checklist.xlsx, perf-test-script.sh

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful and captures the call. A few quick clarifications: 

- Prompt sizes: median ~120 tokens, p95 ~480 tokens (we'll extract an anonymized sample).
- Bursts: our busiest endpoint sees ~700 reqs/min for 10-15 minutes during batch churn; sustained peak closer to 450 reqs/min.
- Cold vs warm cache: we expect many sessions to have warm prefixes (customer profile prompts) but cold starts do happen — we'd like p95 <= 400ms on cold as a softer constraint and p95 <= 300ms for warm cache.

Next steps: I'll get our infra team to sanitize and drop the sample trace in a shared S3 by 2026-03-05. Can we schedule the SE perf run the week of Mar 9? Priyom, any conflicts?

Also confirm that the streaming first-byte target is achievable — the demo showed ~60ms inter-token but our UX team prefers <50ms for the chat feel.

-Appreciate it,
Alex
Head of Product
FintechCo
alex.chen@fintechco.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 07:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Alex — good data points. Quick technical notes / ask so we scope the perf run correctly: 

- For streaming first-byte and inter-token latency, the primary drivers are (1) model choice/quantization profile, (2) CPU/GPU kernel selection for attention, and (3) network e2e to your clients. On Redwood Dedicated we can typically reach ~40-55ms first-byte for small models and ~50-80ms for larger models depending on sequence lengths.

- Given your token distribution (median 120 / p95 480), I recommend we test two model variants: a 13B quantized profile (cost-efficient, lower latency) and a 70B cq4-like profile (higher quality, higher latency). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and streaming inter-token times across both.

- For throughput, we'll run burst tests up to 750 reqs/min and sustained 450 reqs/min with 50 concurrent sessions to validate autoscaler behavior. We'll capture CPU/GPU utilization, queue times, and model-queue latency.

- Please include an example of your longest prompt (anonymized) so we can reproduce tail latency. Also provide an S3 link where we can drop logs from the perf run.

Proposed perf-run window: Mar 9-10, 2026. Marissa — can you confirm Redwood staging Dedicated capacity for those dates?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fintechco.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

That sounds like a good plan — thanks Priyom. We can get the anonymized sample traffic and the longest prompt into S3 by EOD Mar 5. Marissa — please reserve the staging Dedicated slot Mar 9-10; Sean, loop in finance if we need a short commit for a staging pool.

On streaming: we'll accept a soft target of <50ms first-byte for the smaller model and understand the larger model may be ~60-80ms. If the 13B hits your p95 targets, we'll use it for initial pilot and re-evaluate quality.

Confirming owners: Alex (sample traffic, 3/5), Priyom (perf run, 3/10), Marissa (SLO checklist shared), Sean (commercial alignment).

Looking forward.
Alex
